historical_demand_investigations.observation: Dementia has materially higher normalized interest than the other two across the displayed period; B12 is volatile and lower. No publication-specific traffic inference is supported.
Dehydration dominates and shows a pronounced seasonal spike; anticholinergic is comparatively tiny. This supports broad seasonal demand, not a claim that search caused views.
Normalized interest is volatile with intermittent peaks; no clear unique spike at the February 2025 BHWA publication is visible at this resolution.

Medicare shows recurring sharp seasonal peaks; constipation is steadier and substantial; osteoporosis rises gradually; urinary incontinence is lower. Normalized comparison cannot supply absolute searches.

external_comparable_video_research.observation: Older, shorter caregiver explainer existed a decade before BHWA and had meaningful but much lower public reach. Age/channel/length differ; count does not prove creative inferiority.

external_comparable_video_research.title: Doctor explains Vitamin B12 Deficiency | Causes, Symptoms, Foods, Treatment and more!
external_comparable_video_research.observation: Closely related clinician explainer appeared about one month before BHWA, confirming active competition. Comparable public view count was not verified, so no winner claim.

external_comparable_video_research.title: Doctor Explains: 9 Common Medications That May Increase Dementia Risk
external_comparable_video_research.observation: Later, smaller medical channel achieved substantial public reach with nearly same medication-memory promise. Supports durable topic demand; later date and channel context block causal comparison.

external_comparable_video_research.title: The physician's Alzheimer's disease management guide
external_comparable_video_research.observation: External clinical literature supports distinction and multiple-cause framing. Not a YouTube performance comparator; used only for topic/evidence context.

medical_claim_reviews.claim: Anticholinergic drugs can impair cognition in older adults; medication changes require clinician review.
medical_claim_reviews.note: NIA supports confusion/memory effects and professional review. Observational dementia associations do not prove that any individual drug caused dementia.

medical_claim_reviews.claim: Older adults are at risk of B12 deficiency; MMA can clarify borderline status; high-dose oral therapy can be effective.
medical_claim_reviews.note: NIH supports risk, symptoms and oral treatment evidence but notes low-quality RCT evidence; B12 does not generally improve cognition absent deficiency.

medical_claim_reviews.claim: Routine high-dose vitamin D and routine testing are not justified for healthy 50–74-year-olds; lower daily doses preferred when indicated.
medical_claim_reviews.note: Guideline separately suggests empiric supplementation for adults 75+; ‘less is more’ needs this age distinction.

medical_claim_reviews.claim: Long-term NSAIDs can cause bleeding or kidney harm and may be unsafe for many older adults.
medical_claim_reviews.note: No single OTC analgesic is safest for every person; liver disease, kidney disease, bleeding, cardiovascular use and dose matter.

medical_claim_reviews.claim: Do not screen for or treat asymptomatic bacteriuria in most older adults; delirium/falls alone require other-cause assessment.
medical_claim_reviews.note: Exceptions and systemic instability require clinical judgment; transcript appropriately avoids absolute no-treatment advice.

medical_claim_reviews.claim: Orthostatic hypotension is a sustained >=20/10 mmHg fall within 3 minutes standing and is common with age.
medical_claim_reviews.note: Individual BP targets remain contextual; video’s symptom/medication emphasis is defensible.

medical_claim_reviews.claim: Adults 65+ are more heat-vulnerable, may not adjust well, and should not wait for thirst in hot weather.
medical_claim_reviews.note: CDC explicitly says people on fluid limits/diuretics should ask clinicians how much to drink.

medical_claim_reviews.claim: Approved osteoporosis medicines can reduce fracture risk; drug choice and sequencing depend on risk.
medical_claim_reviews.note: Rare harms and drug holidays require individualized management; lifestyle alone is not equivalent after high-risk fracture.
